pattern_id: Statement ordering bug - comparing variable before assignment causes highTC never updated
description: BUG PATTERN: Statement Ordering Bug - Comparison Before Assignment. DESCRIPTION: In Synchronizer.AdvanceView(), the variable v is compared against s.highTC.View() before being assigned the actual tc.View() value. Since v is initialized to 0, the comparison 'v > s.highTC.View()' is always false (unless highTC is negative, which is impossible), causing highTC to never be updated with new timeout certificates. ROOT CAUSE: Code ordering mistake - the assignment 'v = tc.View()' appears AFTER the comparison that uses v. The developer likely intended to first extract the view from the TC, then compare it. INCORRECT CODE: 'v := 0; if v > s.highTC.View() { s.highTC = tc }; v = tc.View()'. CORRECT CODE: 'v = tc.View(); if v > s.highTC.View() { s.highTC = tc }'. IMPACT: Timeout certificates are never recorded as the new highTC, potentially breaking view synchronization. Nodes may fail to advance views properly during timeout scenarios, affecting liveness. FIX: Move 'v = tc.View()' before the comparison. LESSON: When comparing values derived from input data, always extract/assign the value before using it in comparisons. This pattern of 'initialize to zero, compare, then assign' is a common source of bugs. Code review should check that variables used in comparisons have been properly initialized with meaningful values.
